item.title: Six in ten women say they were denied adequate care after miscarriage, new Miscarriage Association research reveals - The Miscarriage Association
item.description: Our major new report, Miscarriage in the UK, published in March 2026, reveals that more than six in ten women (65%) say they did not receive adequate follow-up care after miscarriage. item.description: For many people, Mother’s Day is a time of celebration. A day filled with cards, flowers and messages of appreciation. item.description: The UK Covid-19 Inquiry has today (19 March) published its third report looking at what happened to the NHS and health services during the pandemic, including shedding light on how restrictions affected access to pregnancy care at the time. item.title: Scottish Government publishes miscarriage patient charter - The Miscarriage Association
item.description: On Friday 20 March, the Scottish Government confirmed that Scotland will become the first country in the UK to introduce a miscarriage patient charter, providing clear information on the care and support people can expect from NHS services. item.description: The UK Government has published a new Pandemic Preparedness Strategy, setting out how the country will strengthen its response to future health emergencies, backed by around £1 billion of investment in health protection measures. item.title: Pregnancy after miscarriage: Holding hope and fear at the same time - The Miscarriage Association
item.description: For many people, seeing a positive pregnancy test brings excitement, joy and anticipation. But when you’ve experienced miscarriage before, a new pregnancy can feel very different. item.title: Northern Ireland offers two weeks paid bereavement leave to those affected by pregnancy loss - The Miscarriage Association
item.description: Starting on 6 April, women and their partners affected by pregnancy loss in Northern Ireland will be offered two weeks paid bereavement leave.
